147	
148	def _validate_selection(value: object, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
149	    if not isinstance(value, dict) \
150	            or set(value.keys()) != set(_SELECTION_FIELDS):
151	        raise ValueError(f"{label} has invalid fields")
152	    resource_id = value["resource_id"]
153	    version = value["version"]
154	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
155	        raise ValueError(f"{label} resource_id must be a non-empty string")
156	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
157	        raise ValueError(f"{label} version must be a positive integer")
158	    return {"resource_id": resource_id, "version": version}
159	
160	
161	def _validate_candidate(
162	    entry: object,
163	    work: int,
164	    at: int,
165	    job: dict[str, Any],
166	    current: dict[str, Any],
167	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
168	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
169	    seen: set[str],
170	) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
171	    if not isinstance(entry, dict) \
172	            or set(entry.keys()) != set(_CANDIDATE_FIELDS):
173	        raise ValueError("advice candidate has invalid fields")
174	    resource = entry["resource"]
175	    signal = entry["signal"]
176	    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
177	            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_resources._RECORD_FIELDS):
178	        raise ValueError("advice candidate resource has invalid fields")
179	    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
180	    version = resource["version"]
181	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
182	        raise ValueError("advice candidate resource_id must be a non-empty "
183	                         "string")
184	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
185	        raise ValueError("advice candidate version must be a positive "
186	                         "integer")
187	    # The versioned record must be the exact, immutable supply record.
188	    records = history.get(resource_id)
189	    if records is None or version > len(records) \
190	            or dict(resource) != records[version - 1]:
191	        raise ValueError("advice candidate must reference a published "
192	                         "resource version")
193	    if resource_id in seen:
194	        raise ValueError("advice candidates must be distinct resources")
195	    seen.add(resource_id)
196	    # The retained item is the trade's frozen version; a migration item
197	    # may only be another resource's highest version valid at at -- never
198	    # a different version of the current resource.
199	    if resource_id == current["resource_id"]:
200	        if version != current["version"]:
201	            raise ValueError("advice retained candidate must use the "
202	                             "trade's frozen resource version")
203	    else:
204	        # The construction path picks the resource's highest version
205	        # valid at at; like a frozen trade candidate, a later supply
206	        # publication must not invalidate the recorded advice, so on
207	        # readback only the frozen version's own window is checked.
208	        if not resource["start"] <= at <= resource["end"]:
209	            raise ValueError("advice migration candidate must be valid at "
210	                             "the evaluation moment")
211	    if resource["region"] not in set(job["regions"]):
212	        raise ValueError("advice candidate is outside the job's regions")
213	    if not set(job["residency"]) <= set(resource["residency"]):
214	        raise ValueError("advice candidate does not cover job residency")
215	    if resource["end"] < job["deadline"]:
216	        raise ValueError("advice candidate does not cover the job deadline")
217	    # Validate a copy: _check_values normalizes the mix order in place,
218	    # and the parsed record's raw key order must survive for the
219	    # canonical-byte comparison.
220	    if not isinstance(signal, dict) \
221	            or set(signal.keys()) != set(_signals._RECORD_FIELDS):
222	        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal has invalid fields")
223	    signal_copy = dict(signal)
224	    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
225	    _signals._check_values(signal_copy)
226	    if signal["region"] != resource["region"]:
227	        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must cover the resource "
228	                         "region")
229	    signal_records = signal_history.get(resource["region"])
230	    if signal_records is None or signal["version"] > len(signal_records) \
231	            or dict(signal) != signal_records[signal["version"] - 1]:
232	        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must reference a "
233	                         "published signal version")
234	    if not (signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]):
235	        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must be valid at the "
236	                         "evaluation moment")
237	    total_cost = entry["total_cost"]
238	    total_carbon = entry["total_carbon"]
239	    if not _is_plain_int(total_cost) or total_cost < 0 \
240	            or total_cost != work * signal["unit_cost"]:
241	        raise ValueError("advice candidate total_cost is invalid")
242	    if not _is_plain_int(total_carbon) or total_carbon < 0 \
243	            or total_carbon != work * signal["carbon_intensity"]:
244	        raise ValueError("advice candidate total_carbon is invalid")
245	    if total_cost > job["max_cost"] or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
246	        raise ValueError("advice candidate exceeds a job budget")
247	    # Capacity feasibility is a decision-time fact: later trades may
248	    # legitimately fill the version, so like the clearing ledger's
249	    # per-candidate snapshot it is enforced at construction, not on
250	    # readback; advice itself books no capacity.
251	    return signal["carbon_intensity"], signal["unit_cost"], resource_id
252	
253	
254	def _validate_record(
255	    record: object,
256	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
257	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
258	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
259	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
260	) -> dict[str, Any]:
261	    if not isinstance(record, dict) \
262	            or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
263	        raise ValueError("advice record has invalid fields")
264	    job_id = record["job_id"]
265	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
266	        raise ValueError("advice job_id must be a non-empty string")
267	    at = record["at"]
268	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
269	        raise ValueError("advice at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
270	                         "integer")
271	    current = _validate_selection(record["current"], "advice current "
272	                                  "selection")
273	    dispatch = record["dispatch"]
274	    if dispatch not in _DISPATCH_STATES:
275	        raise ValueError("advice dispatch state is invalid")
276	    execution = record["execution"]
277	    if execution not in _EXECUTION_STATES:
278	        raise ValueError("advice execution state is invalid")
279	    recommendation = record["recommendation"]
280	    if recommendation not in _RECOMMENDATIONS:
281	        raise ValueError("advice recommendation is invalid")
282	    target = _validate_selection(record["target"], "advice target")
283	
284	    job = accepted.get(job_id)
285	    if job is None:
286	        raise ValueError("advice record must reference an accepted job")
287	    trade = trades.get(job_id)
288	    if trade is None:
289	        raise ValueError("advice record must reference a recorded trade")
290	    if at > job["deadline"]:
291	        raise ValueError("advice moment must not pass the job deadline")
292	    if current != {"resource_id": trade["resource_id"],
293	                   "version": trade["version"]}:
294	        raise ValueError("advice current selection must match the trade")
295	    # The dispatch and execution states are frozen point-in-time facts:
296	    # a decision keeps evolving after the advice, so the record is
297	    # checked for the state vocabulary only, never against the current
298	    # ledgers (the same way an execution audit snapshot keeps the state
299	    # its action committed).
300	
301	    candidates_raw = record["candidates"]
302	    if not isinstance(candidates_raw, list) or not candidates_raw:
303	        raise ValueError("advice candidates must be a non-empty list")
304	    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
305	    last_rank: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
306	    seen: set[str] = set()
307	    for entry_raw in candidates_raw:
308	        carbon, unit_cost, resource_id = _validate_candidate(
309	            entry_raw, job["work"], at, job, current, history,
310	            signal_history, seen)
311	        rank = (carbon, unit_cost, resource_id)
312	        if last_rank is not None and rank < last_rank:
313	            raise ValueError("advice candidates must be ordered by signal "
314	                             "carbon intensity, unit cost and resource id")
315	        last_rank = rank
316	        candidates.append(copy.deepcopy(entry_raw))
317	
318	    first = candidates[0]["resource"]
319	    first_selection = {"resource_id": first["resource_id"],
320	                       "version": first["version"]}
321	    if target != first_selection:
322	        raise ValueError("advice target must be the first ordered "
323	                         "candidate")
324	    if recommendation == "keep":
325	        if target != current:
326	            raise ValueError("a keep advice must target the current "
327	                             "resource version")
328	    elif target == current:
329	        raise ValueError("a migrate advice must target another resource "
330	                         "version")
331	
332	    return {
333	        "job_id": job_id,
334	        "at": at,
335	        "current": current,
336	        "dispatch": dispatch,
337	        "execution": execution,
338	        "candidates": candidates,
339	        "recommendation": recommendation,
340	        "target": target,

344	def _validate_request(request: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
345	    if not isinstance(request, dict) \
346	            or set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_FIELDS):
347	        raise ValueError("advice request has invalid fields")
348	    job_id = request["job_id"]
349	    at = request["at"]
350	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
351	        raise ValueError("advice request job_id must be a non-empty string")
352	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
353	        raise ValueError("advice request at must be a non-boolean "
354	                         "non-negative integer")
355	    return {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}

358	def _validate_ledger(
359	    data: object,
360	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
361	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
362	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
363	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
364	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
365	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
366	        raise ValueError("advice ledger root must be an object with keys "
367	                         "version, records and audit")
368	    version = data["version"]
369	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
370	        raise ValueError("unsupported advice ledger version")
371	
372	    records_raw = data["records"]
373	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
374	    if not isinstance(records_raw, dict) or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
375	        raise ValueError("records and audit must be objects")
376	    _check_sorted_keys(records_raw, "records")
377	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
378	
379	    # Capacity already sold per exact resource version by every trade is
380	    # a clearing-ledger invariant already enforced when that ledger is
381	    # loaded; advice books nothing itself, so the advice ledger only
382	    # rechecks the frozen supply/signal references, arithmetic and order.
383	    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
384	    for key, record_raw in records_raw.items():
385	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
386	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
387	        record = _validate_record(
388	            record_raw, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
389	        records[key] = record
390	
391	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
392	    for key, event_raw in audit_raw.items():
393	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
394	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
395	        if not isinstance(event_raw, dict) \
396	                or set(event_raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
397	            raise ValueError("advice audit event has invalid fields")
398	        if event_raw["key"] != key or not isinstance(event_raw["key"], str):
399	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
400	        request = _validate_request(event_raw["request"])
401	        result = _validate_record(
402	            event_raw["result"], accepted, trades, history,
403	            signal_history)
404	        if key not in records:
405	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded "
406	                             "advice record")
407	        if result != records[key]:
408	            raise ValueError("audit event result does not match its "
409	                             "record")
410	        if request["job_id"] != result["job_id"] \
411	                or request["at"] != result["at"]:
412	            raise ValueError("audit event request does not match its "
413	                             "record")
414	        events[key] = {"key": key, "request": request, "result": result}
415	
416	    # The two sections describe one advice history: one audit event per
417	    # record and vice versa.
418	    if set(events) != set(records):
419	        raise ValueError("advice records and audit events do not match")
420	    return records, events

423	def _canonical_bytes(
424	    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
425	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
426	) -> bytes:
427	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, sections in their
428	    # fixed field order and records/events keyed by idempotency key in
429	    # code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
430	    payload = {
431	        "version": _VERSION,
432	        "records": {key: records[key] for key in sorted(records)},
433	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
434	    }
435	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
436	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
437	    return text.encode("utf-8")

440	def _load_ledger(
441	    realpath: str,
442	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
443	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
444	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
445	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
446	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
447	    try:
448	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
449	            raw = handle.read()
450	    except FileNotFoundError:
451	        return {}, {}, None
452	    try:
453	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
454	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
455	        raise ValueError(
456	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
457	    try:
458	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
459	        data = finite_loads(text)
460	    except ValueError as exc:
461	        raise ValueError(
462	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
463	    records, events = _validate_ledger(
464	        data, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
465	    # As for the other ledgers, the ledger is accepted only in canonical
466	    # compact form with a single trailing newline.
467	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(records, events):
468	        raise ValueError(
469	            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
470	    return records, events, raw

473	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
474	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
475	    try:
476	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
477	    finally:
478	        os.close(dir_fd)

481	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
482	                   first: BaseException) -> None:
483	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
484	    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
485	    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
486	    try:
487	        if old_bytes is None:
488	            try:
489	                os.unlink(realpath)
490	            except FileNotFoundError:
491	                pass
492	        else:
493	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
494	                dir=directory, prefix=".rebalance-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
495	            try:
496	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
497	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
498	                    handle.flush()
499	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
500	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
501	            except BaseException:
502	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
503	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
504	                raise
505	        _fsync_directory(directory)
506	    except OSError as recovery:
507	        raise recovery from first
508	
509	
510	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
511	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
512	    # One durable commit for the record and its audit event: synced
513	    # same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a directory fsync,
514	    # restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure, so an unsuccessful
515	    # evaluation leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit
516	    # event.
517	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
518	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
519	        dir=directory, prefix=".rebalance-", suffix=".tmp")
520	    try:
521	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
522	            handle.write(payload)
523	            handle.flush()
524	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
525	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
526	    except BaseException:
527	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
528	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
529	        raise
530	    try:
531	        _fsync_directory(directory)
532	    except BaseException as first:
533	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
534	        raise

537	def _latest_signal(
538	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
539	    region: str,
540	    at: int,
541	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
542	    # The region's latest observation covering the moment; when several
543	    # windows cover it the highest version wins.
544	    current: dict[str, Any] | None = None
545	    for signal in signal_history.get(region, ()):
546	        if signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]:
547	            current = signal
548	    if current is None:
549	        return None
550	    signal_copy = dict(current)
551	    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(current["mix"])
552	    return signal_copy

555	def evaluate(
556	    jobs: str,
557	    supply: str,
558	    signals: str,
559	    trades: str,
560	    dispatch: str,
561	    execution: str,
562	    ledger: str,
563	    job_id: str,
564	    key: str,
565	    at: int,
566	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
567	    """Re-evaluate one unfinished trade and advise keep or migrate.
568	
569	    The seven paths, ``job_id`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings
570	    and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment; the
571	    seven paths must also resolve to distinct real locations. Any
572	    violation raises ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.
573	
574	    The acceptance, supply, signal, clearing, dispatch and execution
575	    files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks together
576	    with the advice ledger's exclusive lock, all seven taken in
577	    resolved real-path order. The retained candidate is the exact
578	    resource version the job's trade froze; every migration candidate is
579	    another resource's highest supply version valid at ``at``. Each
580	    candidate must sit in one of the job's regions, cover its residency,
581	    stay available until the deadline and price within both budgets on
582	    the region's latest signal valid at ``at`` -- a region without such
583	    a signal contributes nothing. Capacity is deducted per exact
584	    resource version for every trade other jobs booked; this job's own
585	    trade is never deducted against itself. Candidates are ordered by
586	    signal carbon intensity, signal unit cost and resource id.
587	
588	    Advice is refused, in this order, when the dispatch decision has
589	    already succeeded or any execution plan has completed
590	    (``ValueError``), when an execution plan is still active
591	    (``PermissionError``) and when ``at`` is past the job deadline
592	    (``TimeoutError``); none of these writes. With no feasible candidate
593	    the call raises ``LookupError`` without writing.
594	
595	    Returns ``(record, created)``. The record freezes, in order, the job
596	    id, the evaluation moment, the current selection, the dispatch and
597	    execution states, the ordered candidates, the recommendation
598	    (``keep`` when the first candidate is the current version, otherwise
599	    ``migrate``) and the target selection. A missing advice ledger is
600	    created only by the first record, the record and its audit event
601	    committed together in one synced atomic write. Replaying the same
602	    key with the same job and moment returns the stored record with
603	    ``False`` without writing; the same key with a changed request
604	    raises ``ValueError`` and leaves the ledger untouched.
605	
606	    An unknown job or dispatch decision raises ``KeyError``; a job
607	    without a trade and an empty feasible set raise ``LookupError``;
608	    neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or the ledger parent
609	    raise ``FileNotFoundError``; invalid arguments, structure, ordering,
610	    references or non-canonical bytes raise ``ValueError``; other
611	    locking, read/write or sync failures raise ``OSError``.
612	    """
613	    for value in (jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution,
614	                  ledger, job_id, key):
615	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
616	            raise ValueError("the seven paths, job_id and key must be "
617	                             "non-empty strings")
618	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
619	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
620	
621	    job_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
622	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply)
623	    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signals)
624	    trades_real = os.path.realpath(trades)
625	    dispatch_real = os.path.realpath(dispatch)
626	    execution_real = os.path.realpath(execution)
627	    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
628	    all_paths = (job_real, supply_real, signal_real, trades_real,
629	                 dispatch_real, execution_real, ledger_real)
630	    if len(set(all_paths)) != 7:
631	        raise ValueError("the seven paths must be distinct real paths")
632	
633	    store = _get_store(ledger)
634	    with store.lock:
635	        # Locks are taken in one resolved-real-path order shared by every
636	        # caller, so concurrent evaluations can never deadlock; the
637	        # advice ledger lock is exclusive, the six snapshot locks shared.
638	        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
639	            for locked in sorted(set(all_paths)):
640	                stack.enter_context(
641	                    _lock(locked, shared=(locked != ledger_real)))
642	
643	            accepted, job_map, job_events, job_raw = \
644	                _jobs._load_submit_file(job_real)
645	            if job_raw is None:
646	                raise FileNotFoundError(
647	                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
648	            if job_raw != _jobs._serialize_submit_file(
649	                    accepted, job_map, job_events):
650	                raise ValueError(
651	                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} is not in canonical "
652	                    "compact form")
653	            history, _supply_map, _supply_events, supply_raw = \
654	                _resources._load_file(supply_real)
655	            if supply_raw is None:
656	                raise FileNotFoundError(
657	                    f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
658	            signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
659	                _signals._load_file(signal_real)
660	            if signal_raw is None:
661	                raise FileNotFoundError(
662	                    f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")
663	            # Live trades freeze signal versions, so the signal history
664	            # resolves their references; static trades validate as before.
665	            cleared, _clear_keys, trades_raw = _market._load_clear_ledger(
666	                trades_real, accepted, history, signal_history)
667	            if trades_raw is None:
668	                raise FileNotFoundError(
669	                    f"clearing ledger {trades_real!r} does not exist")
670	            decisions, _dispatch_keys, _dispatch_events, dispatch_raw = \
671	                _dispatch._load_ledger(dispatch_real)
672	            if dispatch_raw is None:
673	                raise FileNotFoundError(
674	                    f"dispatch ledger {dispatch_real!r} does not exist")
675	            # The execution ledger is a required input, as in the other
676	            # layers that read it: advice presupposes a claim, and the
677	            # natural re-evaluation point is a job whose prior execution
678	            # attempt failed or was interrupted (its plan history frozen
679	            # in this ledger). A missing file is FileNotFoundError.
680	            plans, _plan_keys, _plan_events = \
681	                _execution._load_existing_ledger(execution_real)[:3]
682	            records, events, old_bytes = _load_ledger(
683	                ledger_real, accepted, cleared, history, signal_history)
684	
685	            request = {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}
686	            binding = records.get(key)
687	            if binding is not None:
688	                if binding["job_id"] != job_id or binding["at"] != at:
689	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
690	                                     "a different request")
691	                # An equivalent replay returns the stored record without
692	                # re-evaluating or rewriting a byte.
693	                return copy.deepcopy(binding), False
694	
695	            job = accepted.get(job_id)
696	            if job is None:
697	                raise KeyError(job_id)
698	            trade = cleared.get(job_id)
699	            if trade is None:
700	                raise LookupError("job has no recorded trade")
701	            decision = decisions.get(job_id)
702	            if decision is None:
703	                raise KeyError(job_id)
704	
705	            job_plans = plans.get(job_id, {})
706	            # Refusal order is fixed: a finished booking is a ValueError,
707	            # work still in flight is a PermissionError, and a moment
708	            # past the deadline is a TimeoutError.
709	            if decision["state"] == "succeeded" \
710	                    or any(plan["state"] == "completed"
711	                           for plan in job_plans.values()):
712	                raise ValueError("a finished booking cannot be "
713	                                 "re-evaluated")
714	            if any(plan["state"] == "active"
715	                   for plan in job_plans.values()):
716	                raise PermissionError("an execution plan is active")
717	            if at > job["deadline"]:
718	                raise TimeoutError("evaluation moment exceeds the job "
719	                                   "deadline")
720	
721	            current_id = trade["resource_id"]
722	            current_version = trade["version"]
723	            current = {"resource_id": current_id,
724	                       "version": current_version}
725	            work = job["work"]
726	            regions = set(job["regions"])
727	            residency = set(job["residency"])
728	
729	            # Capacity already booked per exact resource version by
730	            # every OTHER job; this job's own frozen occupancy is never
731	            # deducted against itself.
732	            booked: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
733	            for other_id, other in cleared.items():
734	                if other_id == job_id:
735	                    continue
736	                slot = (other["resource_id"], other["version"])
737	                booked[slot] = booked.get(slot, 0) + other["work"]
738	
739	            candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
740	
741	            def consider(resource_record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
742	                if resource_record["region"] not in regions:
743	                    return
744	                if not residency <= set(resource_record["residency"]):
745	                    return
746	                if resource_record["end"] < job["deadline"]:
747	                    return
748	                signal = _latest_signal(
749	                    signal_history, resource_record["region"], at)
750	                if signal is None:
751	                    return
752	                remaining = resource_record["capacity"] - booked.get(
753	                    (resource_record["resource_id"],
754	                     resource_record["version"]), 0)
755	                if remaining < work:
756	                    return
757	                total_cost = work * signal["unit_cost"]
758	                total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]
759	                if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
760	                        or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
761	                    return
762	                candidates.append({
763	                    "resource": dict(resource_record),
764	                    "signal": signal,
765	                    "total_cost": total_cost,
766	                    "total_carbon": total_carbon,
767	                })
768	
769	            # The retained item is the immutable version the trade froze,
770	            # independent of whether its supply window is still open.
771	            frozen_records = history.get(current_id)
772	            if frozen_records is None or current_version > len(frozen_records):
773	                raise ValueError("trade references an unpublished "
774	                                 "resource version")
775	            consider(frozen_records[current_version - 1])
776	
777	            # Migration items: only other resources' highest versions
778	            # valid at the moment -- never another version of the current
779	            # resource.
780	            for resource_id, versions in history.items():
781	                if resource_id == current_id:
782	                    continue
783	                active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
784	                for version_record in versions:
785	                    if version_record["start"] <= at <= version_record["end"]:
786	                        active = version_record
787	                if active is None:
788	                    continue
789	                consider(active)
790	
791	            candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
792	                entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
793	                entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
794	                entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
795	            if not candidates:
796	                raise LookupError("no feasible resource for the job at "
797	                                  "the evaluation moment")
798	
799	            winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
800	            target = {"resource_id": winner["resource_id"],
801	                      "version": winner["version"]}
802	            recommendation = ("keep" if target == current else "migrate")
803	            if job_plans:
804	                execution_state = max(
805	                    job_plans.values(),
806	                    key=lambda plan: plan["attempt"])["state"]
807	            else:
808	                execution_state = "none"
809	
810	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
811	                "job_id": job_id,
812	                "at": at,
813	                "current": current,
814	                "dispatch": decision["state"],
815	                "execution": execution_state,
816	                "candidates": candidates,
817	                "recommendation": recommendation,
818	                "target": target,
819	            }
820	            records[key] = record
821	            events[key] = {"key": key, "request": dict(request),
822	                           "result": copy.deepcopy(record)}
823	            _commit_file(ledger_real,
824	                         _canonical_bytes(records, events), old_bytes)
825	            return copy.deepcopy(record), True

"""Persistent re-evaluation and migration advice for booked trades.

The market already books a job against one exact resource version
(``market.clear``/``market.clear_live``), dispatch commits and claims
that decision and the execution layer runs launch or migration plans,
while the live signal ledger keeps publishing fresh region observations.
What is missing until this module is a re-evaluation of an unfinished
booking: given the signals valid *now*, should the job stay on the
resource version its trade froze, or migrate to another resource whose
current version is cleaner or cheaper right now?

:func:`evaluate` is the one and only public call. It reads the seven
layers -- the ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the resource supply file,
the live signal file, the ``market.clear`` clearing ledger, the dispatch
ledger, the execution ledger and this module's advice ledger -- as one
snapshot under their shared locks together with the advice ledger's
exclusive lock, all seven taken in resolved real-path order, so
concurrent calls across processes can never deadlock.

The re-evaluation rules are deliberately asymmetric between the slot
the job already occupies and every alternative:

* the retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade
  froze, even once that version's own supply window has closed -- the
  job is already running on it;
* a migration item uses only another resource's highest version valid
  at the evaluation moment, never another version of the same resource;
* every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later
  than the moment and not expired at it, and keeps the job's region,
  residency, deadline, cost and carbon budgets;
* capacity is deducted per exact resource version from every trade
  other jobs booked, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never
  deducted twice.

Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit
cost, then resource id. When the first item is still the traded version
the advice is ``keep``; otherwise it is ``migrate`` to that first item.

Advice is refused while the booking is past re-evaluation: a succeeded
dispatch decision or a completed execution plan raises ``ValueError``,
an active execution plan raises ``PermissionError`` and an evaluation
moment past the job deadline raises ``TimeoutError`` -- in that order,
and none of them writes advice. An unknown job or dispatch decision
raises ``KeyError`` and a job without a trade, or one with no feasible
item, raises ``LookupError``; neither creates the ledger.

The advice ledger (version 1) holds ``records`` keyed by idempotency
key and one ``audit`` event per first-served key; both sections are
ordered by key code point. A first evaluation returns
``(record, True)``; replaying the same key with the same job and
evaluation moment returns the stored record with ``False`` without
writing, while the same key with a changed request raises
``ValueError``. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be exactly the
canonical compact form :func:`_canonical_bytes` produces -- compact
UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or
non-finite number literals and exactly one trailing newline -- and
every commit goes through a synced same-directory temporary file, an
atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on
failure, so an unsuccessful call leaves neither a temporary fragment
nor half an audit event.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import copy
import fcntl
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from . import dispatch as _dispatch
from . import execution as _execution
from . import jobs as _jobs
from . import market as _market
from . import resources as _resources
from . import signals as _signals
from ._jsonio import finite_loads

__all__ = ["evaluate"]

_VERSION = 1
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "records", "audit")
_RECORD_FIELDS = ("job_id", "at", "current", "dispatch", "execution",
                  "candidates", "recommendation", "target")
_SELECTION_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version")
_CANDIDATE_FIELDS = ("resource", "signal", "total_cost", "total_carbon")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "request", "result")
_REQUEST_FIELDS = ("job_id", "at")
_DISPATCH_STATES = ("ready", "claimed", "succeeded", "failed")
_EXECUTION_STATES = ("none", "active", "completed", "failed",
                     "interrupted")
_RECOMMENDATIONS = ("keep", "migrate")
_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # As in the other ledgers, the companion lock file is never unlinked
    # and an flock is released by the kernel on process exit, so
    # equivalent real paths share one lock across threads, processes and
    # modules.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def _validate_selection(value: object, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(value, dict) \
            or set(value.keys()) != set(_SELECTION_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} has invalid fields")
    resource_id = value["resource_id"]
    version = value["version"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} version must be a positive integer")
    return {"resource_id": resource_id, "version": version}


def _validate_candidate(
    entry: object,
    work: int,
    at: int,
    job: dict[str, Any],
    current: dict[str, Any],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    seen: set[str],
) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) \
            or set(entry.keys()) != set(_CANDIDATE_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate has invalid fields")
    resource = entry["resource"]
    signal = entry["signal"]
    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_resources._RECORD_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate resource has invalid fields")
    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
    version = resource["version"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate resource_id must be a non-empty "
                         "string")
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate version must be a positive "
                         "integer")
    # The versioned record must be the exact, immutable supply record.
    records = history.get(resource_id)
    if records is None or version > len(records) \
            or dict(resource) != records[version - 1]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate must reference a published "
                         "resource version")
    if resource_id in seen:
        raise ValueError("advice candidates must be distinct resources")
    seen.add(resource_id)
    # The retained item is the trade's frozen version; a migration item
    # may only be another resource's highest version valid at at -- never
    # a different version of the current resource.
    if resource_id == current["resource_id"]:
        if version != current["version"]:
            raise ValueError("advice retained candidate must use the "
                             "trade's frozen resource version")
    else:
        # The construction path picks the resource's highest version
        # valid at at; like a frozen trade candidate, a later supply
        # publication must not invalidate the recorded advice, so on
        # readback only the frozen version's own window is checked.
        if not resource["start"] <= at <= resource["end"]:
            raise ValueError("advice migration candidate must be valid at "
                             "the evaluation moment")
    if resource["region"] not in set(job["regions"]):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate is outside the job's regions")
    if not set(job["residency"]) <= set(resource["residency"]):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate does not cover job residency")
    if resource["end"] < job["deadline"]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate does not cover the job deadline")
    # Validate a copy: _check_values normalizes the mix order in place,
    # and the parsed record's raw key order must survive for the
    # canonical-byte comparison.
    if not isinstance(signal, dict) \
            or set(signal.keys()) != set(_signals._RECORD_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal has invalid fields")
    signal_copy = dict(signal)
    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
    _signals._check_values(signal_copy)
    if signal["region"] != resource["region"]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must cover the resource "
                         "region")
    signal_records = signal_history.get(resource["region"])
    if signal_records is None or signal["version"] > len(signal_records) \
            or dict(signal) != signal_records[signal["version"] - 1]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must reference a "
                         "published signal version")
    if not (signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]):
        raise ValueError("advice candidate signal must be valid at the "
                         "evaluation moment")
    total_cost = entry["total_cost"]
    total_carbon = entry["total_carbon"]
    if not _is_plain_int(total_cost) or total_cost < 0 \
            or total_cost != work * signal["unit_cost"]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate total_cost is invalid")
    if not _is_plain_int(total_carbon) or total_carbon < 0 \
            or total_carbon != work * signal["carbon_intensity"]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate total_carbon is invalid")
    if total_cost > job["max_cost"] or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
        raise ValueError("advice candidate exceeds a job budget")
    # Capacity feasibility is a decision-time fact: later trades may
    # legitimately fill the version, so like the clearing ledger's
    # per-candidate snapshot it is enforced at construction, not on
    # readback; advice itself books no capacity.
    return signal["carbon_intensity"], signal["unit_cost"], resource_id


def _validate_record(
    record: object,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(record, dict) \
            or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice record has invalid fields")
    job_id = record["job_id"]
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("advice job_id must be a non-empty string")
    at = record["at"]
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("advice at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                         "integer")
    current = _validate_selection(record["current"], "advice current "
                                  "selection")
    dispatch = record["dispatch"]
    if dispatch not in _DISPATCH_STATES:
        raise ValueError("advice dispatch state is invalid")
    execution = record["execution"]
    if execution not in _EXECUTION_STATES:
        raise ValueError("advice execution state is invalid")
    recommendation = record["recommendation"]
    if recommendation not in _RECOMMENDATIONS:
        raise ValueError("advice recommendation is invalid")
    target = _validate_selection(record["target"], "advice target")

    job = accepted.get(job_id)
    if job is None:
        raise ValueError("advice record must reference an accepted job")
    trade = trades.get(job_id)
    if trade is None:
        raise ValueError("advice record must reference a recorded trade")
    if at > job["deadline"]:
        raise ValueError("advice moment must not pass the job deadline")
    if current != {"resource_id": trade["resource_id"],
                   "version": trade["version"]}:
        raise ValueError("advice current selection must match the trade")
    # The dispatch and execution states are frozen point-in-time facts:
    # a decision keeps evolving after the advice, so the record is
    # checked for the state vocabulary only, never against the current
    # ledgers (the same way an execution audit snapshot keeps the state
    # its action committed).

    candidates_raw = record["candidates"]
    if not isinstance(candidates_raw, list) or not candidates_raw:
        raise ValueError("advice candidates must be a non-empty list")
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    last_rank: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for entry_raw in candidates_raw:
        carbon, unit_cost, resource_id = _validate_candidate(
            entry_raw, job["work"], at, job, current, history,
            signal_history, seen)
        rank = (carbon, unit_cost, resource_id)
        if last_rank is not None and rank < last_rank:
            raise ValueError("advice candidates must be ordered by signal "
                             "carbon intensity, unit cost and resource id")
        last_rank = rank
        candidates.append(copy.deepcopy(entry_raw))

    first = candidates[0]["resource"]
    first_selection = {"resource_id": first["resource_id"],
                       "version": first["version"]}
    if target != first_selection:
        raise ValueError("advice target must be the first ordered "
                         "candidate")
    if recommendation == "keep":
        if target != current:
            raise ValueError("a keep advice must target the current "
                             "resource version")
    elif target == current:
        raise ValueError("a migrate advice must target another resource "
                         "version")

    return {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "at": at,
        "current": current,
        "dispatch": dispatch,
        "execution": execution,
        "candidates": candidates,
        "recommendation": recommendation,
        "target": target,
    }


def _validate_request(request: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(request, dict) \
            or set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice request has invalid fields")
    job_id = request["job_id"]
    at = request["at"]
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("advice request job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("advice request at must be a non-boolean "
                         "non-negative integer")
    return {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}


def _validate_ledger(
    data: object,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("advice ledger root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, records and audit")
    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported advice ledger version")

    records_raw = data["records"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(records_raw, dict) or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("records and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(records_raw, "records")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    # Capacity already sold per exact resource version by every trade is
    # a clearing-ledger invariant already enforced when that ledger is
    # loaded; advice books nothing itself, so the advice ledger only
    # rechecks the frozen supply/signal references, arithmetic and order.
    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, record_raw in records_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        record = _validate_record(
            record_raw, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
        records[key] = record

    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, event_raw in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event_raw, dict) \
                or set(event_raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("advice audit event has invalid fields")
        if event_raw["key"] != key or not isinstance(event_raw["key"], str):
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        request = _validate_request(event_raw["request"])
        result = _validate_record(
            event_raw["result"], accepted, trades, history,
            signal_history)
        if key not in records:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded "
                             "advice record")
        if result != records[key]:
            raise ValueError("audit event result does not match its "
                             "record")
        if request["job_id"] != result["job_id"] \
                or request["at"] != result["at"]:
            raise ValueError("audit event request does not match its "
                             "record")
        events[key] = {"key": key, "request": request, "result": result}

    # The two sections describe one advice history: one audit event per
    # record and vice versa.
    if set(events) != set(records):
        raise ValueError("advice records and audit events do not match")
    return records, events


def _canonical_bytes(
    records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, sections in their
    # fixed field order and records/events keyed by idempotency key in
    # code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "records": {key: records[key] for key in sorted(records)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _load_ledger(
    realpath: str,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}, None
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    records, events = _validate_ledger(
        data, accepted, trades, history, signal_history)
    # As for the other ledgers, the ledger is accepted only in canonical
    # compact form with a single trailing newline.
    if raw != _canonical_bytes(records, events):
        raise ValueError(
            f"advice ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
    return records, events, raw


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
                   first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".rebalance-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the record and its audit event: synced
    # same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a directory fsync,
    # restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure, so an unsuccessful
    # evaluation leaves neither a temporary fragment nor half an audit
    # event.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".rebalance-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def _latest_signal(
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    region: str,
    at: int,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    # The region's latest observation covering the moment; when several
    # windows cover it the highest version wins.
    current: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    for signal in signal_history.get(region, ()):
        if signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]:
            current = signal
    if current is None:
        return None
    signal_copy = dict(current)
    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(current["mix"])
    return signal_copy


def evaluate(
    jobs: str,
    supply: str,
    signals: str,
    trades: str,
    dispatch: str,
    execution: str,
    ledger: str,
    job_id: str,
    key: str,
    at: int,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Re-evaluate one unfinished trade and advise keep or migrate.

    The seven paths, ``job_id`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings
    and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment; the
    seven paths must also resolve to distinct real locations. Any
    violation raises ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.

    The acceptance, supply, signal, clearing, dispatch and execution
    files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks together
    with the advice ledger's exclusive lock, all seven taken in
    resolved real-path order. The retained candidate is the exact
    resource version the job's trade froze; every migration candidate is
    another resource's highest supply version valid at ``at``. Each
    candidate must sit in one of the job's regions, cover its residency,
    stay available until the deadline and price within both budgets on
    the region's latest signal valid at ``at`` -- a region without such
    a signal contributes nothing. Capacity is deducted per exact
    resource version for every trade other jobs booked; this job's own
    trade is never deducted against itself. Candidates are ordered by
    signal carbon intensity, signal unit cost and resource id.

    Advice is refused, in this order, when the dispatch decision has
    already succeeded or any execution plan has completed
    (``ValueError``), when an execution plan is still active
    (``PermissionError``) and when ``at`` is past the job deadline
    (``TimeoutError``); none of these writes. With no feasible candidate
    the call raises ``LookupError`` without writing.

    Returns ``(record, created)``. The record freezes, in order, the job
    id, the evaluation moment, the current selection, the dispatch and
    execution states, the ordered candidates, the recommendation
    (``keep`` when the first candidate is the current version, otherwise
    ``migrate``) and the target selection. A missing advice ledger is
    created only by the first record, the record and its audit event
    committed together in one synced atomic write. Replaying the same
    key with the same job and moment returns the stored record with
    ``False`` without writing; the same key with a changed request
    raises ``ValueError`` and leaves the ledger untouched.

    An unknown job or dispatch decision raises ``KeyError``; a job
    without a trade and an empty feasible set raise ``LookupError``;
    neither creates the ledger. Missing input files or the ledger parent
    raise ``FileNotFoundError``; invalid arguments, structure, ordering,
    references or non-canonical bytes raise ``ValueError``; other
    locking, read/write or sync failures raise ``OSError``.
    """
    for value in (jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution,
                  ledger, job_id, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("the seven paths, job_id and key must be "
                             "non-empty strings")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply)
    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signals)
    trades_real = os.path.realpath(trades)
    dispatch_real = os.path.realpath(dispatch)
    execution_real = os.path.realpath(execution)
    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
    all_paths = (job_real, supply_real, signal_real, trades_real,
                 dispatch_real, execution_real, ledger_real)
    if len(set(all_paths)) != 7:
        raise ValueError("the seven paths must be distinct real paths")

    store = _get_store(ledger)
    with store.lock:
        # Locks are taken in one resolved-real-path order shared by every
        # caller, so concurrent evaluations can never deadlock; the
        # advice ledger lock is exclusive, the six snapshot locks shared.
        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
            for locked in sorted(set(all_paths)):
                stack.enter_context(
                    _lock(locked, shared=(locked != ledger_real)))

            accepted, job_map, job_events, job_raw = \
                _jobs._load_submit_file(job_real)
            if job_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
            if job_raw != _jobs._serialize_submit_file(
                    accepted, job_map, job_events):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} is not in canonical "
                    "compact form")
            history, _supply_map, _supply_events, supply_raw = \
                _resources._load_file(supply_real)
            if supply_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
            signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
                _signals._load_file(signal_real)
            if signal_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")
            # Live trades freeze signal versions, so the signal history
            # resolves their references; static trades validate as before.
            cleared, _clear_keys, trades_raw = _market._load_clear_ledger(
                trades_real, accepted, history, signal_history)
            if trades_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"clearing ledger {trades_real!r} does not exist")
            decisions, _dispatch_keys, _dispatch_events, dispatch_raw = \
                _dispatch._load_ledger(dispatch_real)
            if dispatch_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"dispatch ledger {dispatch_real!r} does not exist")
            # The execution ledger is a required input, as in the other
            # layers that read it: advice presupposes a claim, and the
            # natural re-evaluation point is a job whose prior execution
            # attempt failed or was interrupted (its plan history frozen
            # in this ledger). A missing file is FileNotFoundError.
            plans, _plan_keys, _plan_events = \
                _execution._load_existing_ledger(execution_real)[:3]
            records, events, old_bytes = _load_ledger(
                ledger_real, accepted, cleared, history, signal_history)

            request = {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}
            binding = records.get(key)
            if binding is not None:
                if binding["job_id"] != job_id or binding["at"] != at:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different request")
                # An equivalent replay returns the stored record without
                # re-evaluating or rewriting a byte.
                return copy.deepcopy(binding), False

            job = accepted.get(job_id)
            if job is None:
                raise KeyError(job_id)
            trade = cleared.get(job_id)
            if trade is None:
                raise LookupError("job has no recorded trade")
            decision = decisions.get(job_id)
            if decision is None:
                raise KeyError(job_id)

            job_plans = plans.get(job_id, {})
            # Refusal order is fixed: a finished booking is a ValueError,
            # work still in flight is a PermissionError, and a moment
            # past the deadline is a TimeoutError.
            if decision["state"] == "succeeded" \
                    or any(plan["state"] == "completed"
                           for plan in job_plans.values()):
                raise ValueError("a finished booking cannot be "
                                 "re-evaluated")
            if any(plan["state"] == "active"
                   for plan in job_plans.values()):
                raise PermissionError("an execution plan is active")
            if at > job["deadline"]:
                raise TimeoutError("evaluation moment exceeds the job "
                                   "deadline")

            current_id = trade["resource_id"]
            current_version = trade["version"]
            current = {"resource_id": current_id,
                       "version": current_version}
            work = job["work"]
            regions = set(job["regions"])
            residency = set(job["residency"])

            # Capacity already booked per exact resource version by
            # every OTHER job; this job's own frozen occupancy is never
            # deducted against itself.
            booked: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
            for other_id, other in cleared.items():
                if other_id == job_id:
                    continue
                slot = (other["resource_id"], other["version"])
                booked[slot] = booked.get(slot, 0) + other["work"]

            candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

            def consider(resource_record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
                if resource_record["region"] not in regions:
                    return
                if not residency <= set(resource_record["residency"]):
                    return
                if resource_record["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                    return
                signal = _latest_signal(
                    signal_history, resource_record["region"], at)
                if signal is None:
                    return
                remaining = resource_record["capacity"] - booked.get(
                    (resource_record["resource_id"],
                     resource_record["version"]), 0)
                if remaining < work:
                    return
                total_cost = work * signal["unit_cost"]
                total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]
                if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
                        or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                    return
                candidates.append({
                    "resource": dict(resource_record),
                    "signal": signal,
                    "total_cost": total_cost,
                    "total_carbon": total_carbon,
                })

            # The retained item is the immutable version the trade froze,
            # independent of whether its supply window is still open.
            frozen_records = history.get(current_id)
            if frozen_records is None or current_version > len(frozen_records):
                raise ValueError("trade references an unpublished "
                                 "resource version")
            consider(frozen_records[current_version - 1])

            # Migration items: only other resources' highest versions
            # valid at the moment -- never another version of the current
            # resource.
            for resource_id, versions in history.items():
                if resource_id == current_id:
                    continue
                active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
                for version_record in versions:
                    if version_record["start"] <= at <= version_record["end"]:
                        active = version_record
                if active is None:
                    continue
                consider(active)

            candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
                entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
                entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
                entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
            if not candidates:
                raise LookupError("no feasible resource for the job at "
                                  "the evaluation moment")

            winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
            target = {"resource_id": winner["resource_id"],
                      "version": winner["version"]}
            recommendation = ("keep" if target == current else "migrate")
            if job_plans:
                execution_state = max(
                    job_plans.values(),
                    key=lambda plan: plan["attempt"])["state"]
            else:
                execution_state = "none"

            record: dict[str, Any] = {
                "job_id": job_id,
                "at": at,
                "current": current,
                "dispatch": decision["state"],
                "execution": execution_state,
                "candidates": candidates,
                "recommendation": recommendation,
                "target": target,
            }
            records[key] = record
            events[key] = {"key": key, "request": dict(request),
                           "result": copy.deepcopy(record)}
            _commit_file(ledger_real,
                         _canonical_bytes(records, events), old_bytes)
            return copy.deepcopy(record), True
